questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain the following types of business documents;

(i) Catalogue,

(ii) Invoice,

(iii) Credit note.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Catalogue.** A catalogue is a **booklet or list issued by a seller** showing the goods he sells, with descriptions, pictures, catalogue numbers, sizes and prices, and often the terms of sale. It is sent to potential buyers to inform them and to help them order. Example: a wholesaler sends his price catalogue to retailers.

(ii) **Invoice.** An invoice is a document **sent by the seller to the buyer** after goods are sold on credit or delivered. It shows the date, the names and addresses of seller and buyer, the goods (quantity, description, unit price), any trade discount, the total amount **to be paid** and the terms of payment. It is the seller's claim for payment and the buyer's record of the purchase.

(iii) **Credit note.** A credit note is a document **sent by the seller to the buyer** to reduce the amount the buyer owes. It is issued when goods are **returned** (wrong, damaged or excess goods) or when the buyer was **overcharged**. It is often printed in red and shows the goods returned or the amount of the allowance. The buyer's debt is reduced by this amount.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State and explain any FOUR services of a wholesaler to the retailer.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A wholesaler buys goods in large quantities from producers and sells them in smaller quantities to retailers. He is a link between the producer and the retailer and performs these services for retailers.

1. **Breaking bulk.** He buys in large lots from manufacturers and sells in small quantities to retailers, who may not have the money or the space to buy large amounts.
2. **Storage (warehousing).** He keeps stocks in his warehouse, so the retailer does not need a big store and can obtain goods quickly when his own stock is low.
3. **Credit facilities.** He often allows retailers to take goods now and pay later, which helps small retailers who have little capital.
4. **Variety of goods.** He stocks goods from many producers in one place, so a retailer can buy many different goods from one supplier and save time and transport.
5. **Transport and delivery.** Many wholesalers deliver to the retailer's shop, which reduces the retailer's transport costs.
6. **Advice and market information.** He informs retailers about new products, prices and changes in consumers' tastes, and may help with display and advertising.
7. **Risk bearing.** He bears the risk of price changes, damage or loss of the goods while in his warehouse, so the retailer does not.

(Any four services, each stated and explained, earn full marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain FOUR advantages of shopping in a department store.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A department store is a large retail shop divided into departments, each selling a different class of goods (clothes, furniture, electrical goods, food, and so on) under one roof. Shopping there has these advantages.

1. **Wide variety of goods under one roof.** Customers can buy many different things in one visit, which saves time and transport costs.
2. **Convenience and comfort.** There is a pleasant, well-lit place with trolleys, lifts or escalators, restaurants and sometimes toilets and parking.
3. **Competitive prices.** Because the store buys in large quantities, it obtains trade discounts and can often charge lower prices or hold sales.
4. **Quality assurance and after-sales service.** Goods are usually of good quality and the store offers a guarantee, delivery, exchange of goods and repairs.
5. **Credit and payment facilities.** Many stores accept cards or cheques and may offer credit or hire purchase to regular customers.
6. **Attractive display and special offers.** Goods are well displayed and promotions let customers compare goods and enjoy bargains.

(Any four advantages, each explained, earn full marks.)
